lead: A printed page from a 1981 Lithuanian civil-defence training album, drawn and printed like the Soviet Grazhdanskaya Oborona wall charts of 1975-1985: a dark-brown brush-and-ink outline around every figure and object, matte gouache fills with soft shading, four-colour offset lithography with a faint coarse halftone, muted inks of dusty blue, olive, ochre, brick red and grey-brown on warm yellowed dun paper. The dun paper is the background: the main subject is drawn directly on it with its surroundings sketched in around it and fading into the paper at the edges, leaving open margins; insets are small ruled boxes on the same paper. Flat even diagram lighting with a quiet nostalgic warmth. People are ordinary Lithuanians of 1981, anonymous types, sturdily built, with correct natural body proportions. Hair ash-blond, light-brown or chestnut, straight or faintly wavy, some darker; eyes grey, blue-grey or greenish; fair skin. Broad-cheeked oval faces, high straight or humped noses, rounded chins, calm closed mouths, gaze slightly off the viewer. Men side-parted or cropped, some moustached, working men in flat caps; women short-set or in cotton headscarves; plain loose clothes in brown, olive, dusty blue, grey, dull red.
suffix: Finish: muted offset print on warm yellowed dun paper, brush-ink outlines, soft shading, correct body proportions, austere plainly handsome Soviet-era people; diagram arrows and callouts in solid black ink.
